title: HACHIMI-II: From Role-Play to Learner Behavior Modeling for Faithful Student Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2610.19654v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Simulated students let researchers test tutoring systems and teaching strategies before real learners are available, but only if the simulation reproduces where a particular learner succeeds and fails. The common approach asks a large language model to role-play a student, but a role does not model what this learner knows or will do next, so the model's own competence fills the gap. Simulated students perform at a level set by the model, differ little from one another, and seldom make the real learners' errors. We model the learner's behavior and recast student simulation as third-person prediction of the learner's next action. HACHIMI-II builds a student model from the learner's history, infers the learner's state for the current item or tutor turn, and compiles it into a behavior harness that constrains the next action. On three item-response datasets, the Wasserstein-1 distance between simulated and real student ability is 2.4--8.4$\t

translated_title: HACHIMI-II：从角色扮演到学习者行为建模，实现忠实的学生模拟
translated_abstract: 模拟学生使研究人员能够在真实学习者出现之前测试辅导系统和教学策略，但前提是模拟必须重现特定学习者在哪些地方成功、在哪些地方失败。常见做法是让大型语言模型扮演学生角色，但角色设定并不能刻画这个学习者知道什么、下一步会做什么，于是模型自身的能力填补了这一空缺。由此导致模拟学生的表现水平由模型本身决定，彼此之间差异很小，并且很少犯真实学习者会犯的错误。本文对学习者的行为进行建模，将学生模拟重新表述为对学习者下一步动作的第三人称预测。HACHIMI-II 从学习者的历史记录中构建学生模型，推断学习者在当前题目或辅导轮次中的状态，并将其编译成一个约束下一步动作的行为执行框架。在三个题目作答数据集上，模拟学生与真实学生能力之间的 Wasserstein-1 距离为 2.4–8.4（摘要原文在此处截断）。
tldr: HACHIMI-II 将学生模拟从让大语言模型角色扮演转变为对学习者行为的第三人称预测，通过从学习者历史构建学生模型并用行为框架约束其下一步动作，从而忠实再现真实学习者的能力分布和典型错误。
en_tdlr: HACHIMI-II reframes student simulation from LLM role-play to third-person prediction of learner behavior, building a student model from the learner's history and constraining next actions via a behavior harness to faithfully reproduce real learners' abilities and errors.
